notes.meaning: An ancient farmer dug small trenches to steer water anywhere his fields needed it. In the very same way, the Lord has full control over the hearts and minds of kings. Even the most powerful earthly rulers can do only what God allows and directs.

People are quick to justify their own choices and assume their actions are right. But the Lord looks beneath outward excuses and weighs our deepest thoughts and motives. His evaluation of our lives is always completely true and fair.

Doing what is right, fair, and loving toward others pleases the Lord far more than ceremonial rituals. Sacrifices—religious gifts offered to God—mean nothing to Him when offered by people who still mistreat others. God wants heartfelt obedience rather than empty religious shows.

Haughty eyes show the deep arrogance that rules an ungodly heart. When people live only for themselves, even their daily work and successes become sinful. Pride taints everything an unrepentant sinner attempts to do.

Careful planning joined with steady, patient work brings plenty and security. On the other hand, rushing rashly into get-rich-quick schemes leads straight to poverty. Lasting success takes both sound thinking and hard work.

Building wealth by lying, cheating, or making false claims brings no real gain. Dishonest riches blow away as quickly as morning mist or smoke in the wind. Those who chase wealth through fraud are really walking straight toward their own death.

The cruel violence that wicked people inflict on others will eventually drag them away to ruin. Their own crimes act like a saw that cuts them down in the end. This judgment falls on them because they stubbornly refuse to treat people fairly.

A person weighed down by guilt walks a crooked and deceitful path. By contrast, those who are pure in heart live an honest and straightforward life. Our daily conduct reveals whether our hearts are corrupted or clean.

The flat roof of an ancient house was exposed to harsh winds, rain, and heat. Even so, sitting alone in a cramped corner on the roof is better than sharing a spacious house with an argumentative wife. Outer hardship with peace is far better than luxury filled with bitter strife.

An evil person has a constant inner hunger to do harm. Such people show no compassion or pity, not even to friends or neighbors who cross their path. Selfish malice drives away every spark of human kindness.

When a stubborn mocker is punished, simple and naive people take warning and gain wisdom. Wise people, however, do not need severe punishment to learn. They gladly listen to instruction and grow in knowledge without being forced.

God, the Righteous One, watches everything that happens inside the homes of the wicked. Though the ungodly seem to prosper for a time, He will overthrow them and bring them to ruin when their sin is full. Believers should never envy the temporary success of evil people.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Following the Latin Vulgate, some understand the verse to describe a righteous man who watches over the household of the wicked in order to draw them away from evil.

notes.meaning: A person who shuts their ears to the desperate cries of the needy will one day face the same cold silence. When trouble strikes, they will cry out to God for help and receive no answer. God shows mercy to those who show mercy to others.

A discreet, secret gift has great power to calm someone who is boiling with rage. This saying observes how human nature works, but it does not encourage dishonest bribery to corrupt justice. Giving a quiet gift to make peace can often turn away fierce anger.

Godly people feel genuine joy when justice is carried out and right wins. But for those who love doing wrong, the arrival of justice is terrifying. Upright laws bring relief to the faithful while promising ruin to evildoers.

Anyone who wanders off the path of wisdom and sound thinking heads toward destruction. If they do not turn back, their journey ends among the spirits of the dead. Turning away from God's truth leads to lasting ruin and separation from life.

Living only for pleasure, constant partying, and luxury quickly drains a person's savings. Expensive wine and costly oils were common at lavish banquets in Bible times. Putting self-indulgence ahead of hard work and self-control leads straight to poverty.

In God's justice, the wicked often fall into the very traps they planned for the innocent. The righteous are delivered from disaster while the evildoer takes their place, like Haman hanging on the gallows he built for Mordecai. This does not mean the wicked pay for our sins, but that God spares the faithful by judging the guilty.

Living alone in an empty desert with wild beasts and no comfort is harsh and lonely. Yet even that barren isolation is better than sharing a home with an angry, brawling wife. Unchecked temper and bitter arguments ruin the joy of every family bond.

Wise people manage their households well and store up valuable food and oil for the future. A foolish person, however, spends whatever comes in as fast as possible on immediate pleasures. Prudence creates security, while reckless living devours everything.

Whoever eagerly pursues what is right and shows loyal love to others will receive great rewards. God blesses that person with true life, an upright standing, and lasting honor. Seeking God's ways always yields blessings that outlast worldly wealth.

A single wise thinker can conquer a city defended by mighty warriors. Wisdom and careful strategy can tear down strong walls that seemed impossible to breach. Relying on raw human power is useless when matched against godly wisdom.

People who guard their words and control their tongues save themselves from endless trouble. Rash remarks, lies, and angry outbursts often stir up conflicts that cannot be undone. Bridling our speech protects both our lives and our peace of mind.

An arrogant person who looks down on others and treats God with contempt earns the shameful title of mocker. Such people act out of unchecked pride and constantly burst into furious anger. Instead of earning the respect they desire, they bring disgrace upon themselves.

Lazy people continually crave good food and nice things, but their hands refuse to do any real work. Because their desires are never met, they are eaten up inside with frustration, envy, and shame. Refusing to work turns a person's own cravings into a slow, tormenting ruin.

The sluggard wastes the entire day daydreaming and hungering for things he will not work to get. In contrast, the righteous work hard and have plenty to share freely with those in need. Honoring God produces a generous heart, while laziness breeds endless greed.

Sacrifices brought by ungodly people are offensive to the Lord because their lives are full of sin. It is far worse when they offer worship as a disguise for evil plans or to bribe God into overlooking their crimes. God detests religious shows that hide wicked intentions.

A witness who lies in court will eventually be exposed, ruined, and silenced forever. But someone who listens carefully to the facts will speak the truth with confidence, and their word will stand. Truthful speech builds a reliable reputation that outlasts every lie.

An ungodly person puts on a stubborn, shameless face and refuses to blush over their wrongdoing. An upright person, however, thinks carefully about their choices and makes sure their steps follow God's commands. Godly people welcome correction rather than hardening their hearts.

No human wisdom, deep cleverness, or expert advice can ever stand against the Lord. Any plan or scheme that opposes God's sovereign will is doomed to fail completely. To fight against God's purpose is always a losing battle.

Soldiers rightly do their duty by equipping horses and getting ready for the day of battle. Even so, the final victory and true safety come only from the Lord, not from human weapons. We must use the practical tools God gives us, but put our trust in Him alone.
